brief.what: Converts a MIDI performance/DAW export into a readable MuseScore score (orchestral, client: composer Cecilia); has a live web front end for her workflow.
brief.stack: Python >=3.10, uv/pip editable install (music21, partitura, mido, numpy); web front end is stdlib-only Python (web.py) + vanilla JS/CSS, no build step

midi2score/web.py + midi2score/web/ — live web app (server + app.css/app.js/ios.css)
tools/ — CLI harnesses: compare_cue.py, grade_stems.py, notation_census.py, key_accuracy.py, make_h…

conventions: Read README.md then docs/design.md before touching pipeline code; HANDOFF.md holds open work, CLAUDE.md holds only settled invariants
Client data (data/cecilia/*.mscz) is gitignored and never committed; must be dated from zip member timestamps, not trusted at face value
Stave/name comparisons must go through staves.canonical (alias normalizer) or per-stave figures silently collapse and become meaningless
hazards: This is a shared 4-core box — BACKFILL.md throttling rules apply to any bulk/indexing job

components: midi2score/orchestral.py — multi-instrument build: desk splitting, double-track collapsing, orchestral.build
midi2score/staves.py — instrument/stave lexicon, canonicalization, range/synth exclusion rules
midi2score/decisions.py — review-queue question generation from pipeline signals (no learning)
midi2score/web.py + web/store.py/auth.py — multi-account web app: projects, house-style template, sessions
flows: MIDI file → midi2score.pipeline (grid+notevalues) → orchestral.build (stave assignment/merge) → MusicXML/MuseScore output
Uploaded cue via web.py → confirmation surface (desk sizes, stave review) → engrave build → downloadable score in ~/.local/share/midi2score/
Finished .mscz (client's edited score) + original MIDI → tools/compare_cue.py → per-stave/attack/tie comparison report
truth: Runtime project/account data — ~/.local/share/midi2score/ (or $MIDI2SCORE_DATA), never the repo
Client source MIDIs/scores — data/cecilia/*.mscz, gitignored, canonical files named in CLAUDE.md
House style/template — LAFCI Hybrid Score Dorico template, documented in docs/house-style.md
vocabulary: cue — a single piece/section of client score work (e.g. 1M1, 1M3), not a UI element
desk — a stand-pair of players sharing one stave (e.g. Violin 1 desk), distinct from 'track'
stave/staves — a notated instrument line in the output score, assigned via staves.LEXICON merge log…
